full_narration: If fish could breathe on land, why would they still need water? The answer begins with one change, not a whole new fish. Air breathing solves only one problem. The fish still needs water. Its body must handle dry ground. Its fins must support land movement. Water helps many fish survive. Some fish already use air sometimes. Scientists study these changes in survival. A land fish would need many more changes. One ability does not change everything. The big lesson is adaptation. Could another animal change too?
